historical_audit_scope: Eighteen chapter summaries, seventy named statements including examples, reductions and eleven explicitly open problems, and eighty-five subject terms of the v23 source manifest. This is a claim to scoped reader-facing treatment of the full finite index, not a proof that every sentence in the book is reproduced or that all eleven open problems are solved. The separately linked harmonic-density theorem and selected later finite-precision results remain independently sourced.

chapters.title: Boundary observables and reconstruction
chapters.original_summary: Two coupled displacements give a model of a boundary measurement. Averaging over the hidden displacement preserves the measured fluctuations, including a correction missed by simply fixing the hidden displacement at its mean.
chapters.reason: A conditional measurement is computed from an independently fixed energy and contraction; the finite coupled-displacement integral supplies the elementary derivation.

chapters.title: Algebras, modules and combining systems
chapters.original_summary: Knowing how a symmetry acts on one system leaves a question when two systems are put together. A coproduct specifies the joint action. In a finite example from the Ising model, the two sectors being joined must also match.
chapters.reason: A joint symmetry acts through a coproduct. Matching sectors give a finite instance where naive tensoring loses the allowed intermediate state.

chapters.title: Local fields on a curve
chapters.original_summary: The strength of the correlation between two currents grows as their positions approach. Expanding it in powers of the separation gives relations among the harmonics. A small contour around a charged insertion measures the charge.
chapters.reason: The Laurent expansion and weighted residues connect local poles to modal observations and to measurement of a charged source.

chapters.title: Factorization and collision geometry
chapters.original_summary: What data specify a product when several insertion points meet? Four charged lines have the same measured full turns and local dimensions for a whole family of collision rules. Additional symmetry can narrow the choice.
chapters.reason: Consecutive cuts, attachments on the labelled collision slice, and sector-sensitive irregular continuation are distinguished.

chapters.title: Bar constructions and coherent operations
chapters.original_summary: A product turns a word into a shorter word. Recording all the ways to shorten it keeps track of relations among products. The bar and cobar constructions show when this record suffices to reconstruct the algebra.
chapters.reason: Coherent associativity, support, connected duality and the all-arity integrated mode algebra appear as separate results.

chapters.title: Derived adjunctions and induction
chapters.original_summary: An algebraic construction carries a module to another category and back. For current algebras at certain levels, a finite filtration proves that the round trip recovers the original module under specified realization hypotheses. Identifying that construction with a physical interface is a further question.
chapters.reason: The actual unit, generated target and sharp root-length mechanism are given under smooth realization conditions.

chapters.title: Actions and derived centres
chapters.original_summary: A field placed inside a region can act on measurements at the boundary. Acting on the vacuum alone can miss an action that is visible on an excited state. A centre describes operations compatible with all the actions being tested.
chapters.reason: A two-colour family admits full recognition by vacuum evaluation; a separate free half-space construction tests physical observability.

chapters.title: Tensor products, support and completion
chapters.original_summary: A series of vectors need not be a finite sum of vectors times scalar series. This distinction decides whether a spectator can be kept independent when the first two fields are combined.
chapters.reason: The third-state series explains why two separately completed factors have a smaller domain, and why one must compare true intermediate spaces.

chapters.title: Ordered boundary operations and mixed theories
chapters.original_summary: Move two boundary insertions toward the same height while varying their positions along a surface. A contribution concentrated where the positions meet can survive this limit and enter the next operation.
chapters.reason: A height-ordered pole carries a wall term whose differential cancels the simultaneous contact. The chapter retains the many-probe and compact refinements.

chapters.title: Analytic sewing and conformal blocks
chapters.original_summary: Cutting a surface decomposes a correlation into contributions from intermediate states. Sew it back in a different order. The two answers can be compared only where the sums over all intermediate states are defined.
chapters.reason: The positive Virasoro sewing and its genuine input-domain counterexample are distinct from the exactly solvable scalar cylinder.

chapters.title: States, determinant lines and quantum fields
chapters.original_summary: Two states give the same readings on either harmonic alone. A measurement involving both harmonics distinguishes them. A free disk supplies an independent calculation, and cutting a more general filling raises a further normalization problem.
chapters.reason: The neutral disk tomography, charged independent preparation, finite complex amplitude and quadratic continuum result all retain their distinct evidence.

chapters.title: Quantum groups and nonlinear chiral algebras
chapters.original_summary: A symmetry acting on two systems needs a rule for combining its actions. For fields that depend on position, this rule must also respect their exchange. Explicit examples show how many of the field operations the resulting algebra captures.
chapters.reason: A level-changing spectral coproduct, a finite braid algebra, the failed next-order current lift and a computed exceptional quartic exemplify separate results.

chapters.title: Geometric reconstruction and rational examples
chapters.original_summary: Which geometric data recover an algebra of fields? Identifying the vacuum for separated points with its limiting sections at coincident points recovers the original chiral bracket in a specified geometric construction. The category of representations alone can be shared by different algebras.
chapters.reason: The ordinary geometric round trip and the weaker categorical symmetry reconstruction use different actual coefficients.

chapters.title: Branes and open–closed operations
chapters.original_summary: A line can end on a defect, and two endpoints can be joined. A calculation with particle states shows that a flux operation survives the joining even when ordinary multiplication forgets it.
chapters.reason: The joined two-ended particle algebra keeps homological flux and an independent brane field construction has a rigorously proper image at every rank.

chapters.title: Hall geometry and compact states
chapters.original_summary: Count the ways one object can be built as an extension of two others. Keeping the spaces of choices gives a multiplication. For states from a K3 surface, even all the specified traces can miss a nonzero three-state measurement.
chapters.reason: Generated Hall multiplication is independently realized in a specified surface and graph example. The compact relative cubic separates states after a trace loses them.

chapters.title: Arithmetic traces and positivity
chapters.original_summary: The Weil functional assigns a number to a test function using primes and the real place. Moving two copies of a single test farther apart gives a sign question equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis.
chapters.reason: Geometric trace and a positive Hilbert representation compare exactly. The fixed-pulse family states the still open all-test positivity boundary.

chapters.title: From boundary operations to bulk reconstruction
chapters.original_summary: An interface transports observables or states between two descriptions. A filling of the boundary prepares a state. Gluing two filled regions pairs their boundary states. The Gaussian example identifies both a transported operation and a state by measurements made on each side.
chapters.reason: The actual module adjunction, action map, independent preparation and absolute cap are successive obligations. Algebraic kernels in a given precision have their own recipient.

chapters.title: The strongest remaining questions
chapters.original_summary: A test that distinguished the free examples can fail in an interacting theory. The remaining problems specify which collision, composition, state or arithmetic measurement would settle a proposed reconstruction.
chapters.reason: The frontier consists of distinct operation comparisons at collisions, on physical interfaces, at independent completed domains and on a genuine geometric cut; arithmetic positivity is a separate open theorem.
